problem: Which of the following functions is continuous on the interval $[-1,2]?$
worked_solution:
The correct answer is the following. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/e57af2e43bd292195f617f60ffed8055891531a2ca5d0249706497d7932d6639.png)

      

Indeed, this function is continuous on the open intervals $(-\infty ,2)$ and $(2,\infty ).$

Additionally, the function is left-continuous at $x=2.$ Hence, it is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,2].$

So, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty ,2]$ and  $(2,\infty ).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Therefore, this function is continuous on $[-1,2],$ because $[-1,2]$ is contained inside the interval $(-\infty ,2].$

Notice that:

- $g(x)$ and $p(x)$ are not left-continuous at $x=2.$

- $h(x)$ is not defined at $x=-1,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$

- $q(x)$ is not defined at $x=1,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[-1,2].$
